items.title: Why younger generations are worse off than baby boomers
items.description: According to research from the Actuaries Institute, inequality between the younger and older generations is widening and could reach record levels within years.

items.title: 'Gulf War III' pushes gold into bear market with no end in sight
items.description: The gold price is now plunging after the precious metal's surge to a record high this year.

items.title: 'Loophole intact': Crossbenchers slam government's proposed gambling ad reforms
items.description: The partial ad ban will not prevent children from seeing gambling ads during footy or rugby games, Labor's draft legislation shows.

items.title: Live: NSW star in doubt for Origin II after injury in Cronulla's win over Manly
items.description: The Sharks weather a second-half Sea Eagles surge to win 28-22, but lose NSW Origin star Blayke Brailey to a suspected broken arm at Shark Park. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Blues complete famous win over Cats as skipper nails golden moment
items.description: Carlton's resurgence under interim coach Josh Fraser continues, with captain Patrick Cripps securing the Blues a third consecutive victory with a four-point win over Geelong at the MCG. Follow live.

items.title: Protesters taken into custody as police enter camp at Olympic stadium site
items.description: Tensions flared at Victoria Park after police, firefighters and Brisbane City Council officers entered a protest camp ahead of the $3.6 billion Olympic stadium development.

items.title: Tony Abbott elected unopposed as Liberal Party president
items.description: Former prime minister Tony Abbott says he is ready to serve the Liberal Party in its time of 'existential crisis' upon his return to the political stage.

items.title: James Valentine remembered as 'wonderful human being' at public memorial
items.description: The veteran broadcaster's family, friends and loyal listeners gathered in Sydney Town Hall to pay tribute to the 64-year-old who died last month, two years after he was diagnosed with cancer.

items.title: Blue Origin rocket explodes on launch pad during test
items.description: Blue Origin says all personnel are accounted for after experiencing an "anomaly", a term commonly used by rocket companies to describe a launch failure or explosion.

items.title: Romanian expels Russian consul general after drone hits building, wounding two
items.description: A Russian drone has struck an apartment building in NATO-member Romania, wounding two people.

items.title: White House asks Americans to report their neighbours as 'aliens'
items.description: The website features a space-inspired background but its real purpose is to highlight the work of ICE.

items.title: Are you allowed to make deepfakes of the prime minister?
items.description: Are you allowed to make deepfakes of the prime minister?  You might have seen AI generated memes of Albanese on social media following the announcement of the federal budget. Whether or not those are legal comes down to what the post is actually communicating to the people seeing it online.

items.title: Major winemaker considers moving business overseas if tax changes go through
items.description: The managing director of Taylors Wines in South Australia is considering leaving the country in response to the federal government's proposed tax changes.

items.title: Mouse plague forces return of COVID-style restrictions at country WA schools
items.description: COVID-style cleaning measures have returned as WA's ongoing mouse plague spreads across multiple country schools.

items.title: This comedian has 1.7m followers. He doesn't think it's real
items.description: As a comedian with legions of fans on social media, Will Gibb wishes he didn't still feel the need to legitimise himself. But he does.

items.title: Growing garlic is one of life's slower lessons
items.description: In April 2020, I put my first cloves into the ground. Here's what I learnt over the next five years of trying — and often failing — to grow good garlic.

items.title: Our critics can't stop listening to these 10 albums from May
items.description: From long-awaited comebacks to First Nations glam rock and genre-defying polymaths, May was stacked with excellent new releases.

items.title: Farnham says he will not sing on stage again ahead of tribute concert
items.description: Jimmy Barnes, Tina Arena and Human Nature will take the stage to honour Australian legend John Farnham at a Melbourne tribute concert later this year.

items.title: KPMG boss quits amid auditing scandal
items.description: KPMG Australia chief executive Andrew Yates has stepped down amid a scandal involving audit partners accessing confidential client documents.

items.title: Award-winning volunteer charged with possessing child-abuse images
items.description: A former police staffer and lauded SES volunteer is granted bail on a charge of possessing child-abuse images.

items.title: Erin Patterson mushroom trial appeal set after 'miscarriage of justice' claim
items.description: Erin Patterson's appeal against her triple murder conviction will be heard in August, Victoria's Supreme Court has confirmed, with the director of public prosecutions also challenging the length of her jail term.

items.title: Executive defends appointment of 'Pink Ladies' mentee to Sydney council
items.description: A Western Sydney local government executive undermined recruitment processes to hire a woman she mentored for years and socialised with as part of a networking group dubbed the Pink Ladies.

items.title: A 'horror night' of airstrikes leaves southern Lebanese city fearing what's next
items.description: New waves of missile strikes and vast advisories from the Israeli government to evacuate have left residents in Lebanon's south uncertain of where to turn.

items.title: US prosecutor denies launching criminal investigation into E Jean Carroll
items.description: Chicago's top federal prosecutor has denied his office has launched a criminal investigation into E Jean Carroll, who accused Donald Trump of raping her in the mid-1990s.

items.title: Heatwaves unbearable in UK 'built for a climate that no longer exists'
items.description: As the mercury climbed around the United Kingdom this week and new May maximums were recorded in multiple areas, the once-welcome sunshine is sparking alarm among many people.
